name: Zeni Geva
label: Alternative Tentacles
lede: KK Null named his Tokyo band for money and violence, then flew it to Chicago in 1991 to be recorded by Steve Albini. Albini ended up working on five of their records.

eras.title: Null starts a band, then a label
eras.text: KK Null had already done time in the Tokyo noise scene with YBO2 when he started a band with a vocalist, a second guitarist and a drummer from Hanatarash. The name pairs the Japanese word for money with the German word for violence.

years.src: Wikipedia: KK Null · Monumental Movement: Zeni Geva · Trouser Press: Zeni Geva · Bandcamp Daily: Zeni Geva and Beyond
years.h: [[KK Null|9c51604c-a456-4e3e-8f85-cc96ec0df439]] forms Zeni Geva in Tokyo as a quartet
years.p: Null, guitarist Fumiyoshi Suzuki, vocalist Elle and drummer Ikuo Taketani debut with the record How to Kill. It comes out on Null's own NUX Organization label.
years.xp:
Kazuyuki Kishino, born in Tokyo in 1961 and known as KK Null, had joined the noise and progressive rock group YBO2 in 1984 and trained in Butoh dance.

Monumental Movement reads the name as "Zeni" (money) plus "Gewalt" (violence). Trouser Press and the Bandcamp Daily primer both list Taketani, whose résumé also includes Hanatarash and the Boredoms, in the early lineup.

years.h: Mitsuru Tabata joins on guitar and stays 24 years
years.p: Bassist Bunsho Nishikawa replaces Elle, the cassette Vast Impotenz appears, and [[Tatsuya Yoshida|7a82840d-beb5-4819-aed3-6b732332b461]] of [[Ruins|8ca7f2ea-6a8d-412d-a188-f75abea72b67]] briefly takes the drum stool.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates Tabata's arrival to 1988 and his exit to 2012, with a break from 2003 to 2009. Yoshida played for a spell in 1988 and again around 1990 before leaving to concentrate on Ruins.

eras.title: The songs get longer
eras.text: The lineup settled into a trio with no bass, and the songs got longer. It was the sound the West would hear first.

years.src: Scaruffi: Zeni Geva · Wikipedia: Zeni Geva
years.h: Maximum Money Monster opens with a 16-minute track
years.p: Scaruffi hears it as the record where the band stopped sounding like a hardcore group. It's another NUX Organization release.
years.xp: The album was reissued in 2007. A live clip from 1990 with Yoshida on drums is on YouTube.

eras.title: Flights both ways
eras.text: Zeni Geva crossed the Pacific to record with Albini in Chicago, then Albini crossed back to Tokyo the next spring.

years.cap: Total Castration, cover art by Stephen Holman
years.src: Ghost Cult Magazine: Zeni Geva · IDIOTEQ: From Tokyo flyers · Wikipedia: Zeni Geva
years.h: Public Bath flies Zeni Geva to Chicago to record with Steve Albini
years.p: David Hopkins, who runs the label, makes the invitation. They track Total Castration at Albini's home studio, The Basement.
years.xp:
Tabata says the band flew to Chicago in the autumn of 1991 at Hopkins's invitation. Eito Noro was now on drums, replacing Yoshida.

The album is the first of five Zeni Geva records Albini worked on. Skin Graft announced a first-ever vinyl pressing, on gold vinyl, for October 30, 2026. Null said no one would be happier to see it than Hopkins, who died in 2022.

yt: Zeni Geva at the Chameleon, San Francisco, 1992
years.h: Neurosis play the Kennel Club with Zeni Geva and walk away converted
years.p: Steve Von Till of Neurosis on the 1992 San Francisco show that Mason Jones of Charnel Music set up. Neurot signs the band nine years later.
years.xp: Neurot's Deep Cut post credits Jones with the introduction and the Kennel Club gig with winning the label over. Von Till: "After seeing them live and listening to their early records, we were completely blown away." Neurot released 10,000 Light Years in 2001.

years.h: Tabata hands out flyers for Albini's Japan tour outside a Nirvana show
years.p: At Nakano Sunplaza, with Nirvana on the bill inside, he's pushing flyers for Albini's first Japan tour. Albini lands the next month.
years.xp: IDIOTEQ's account of the tour: Albini played Shinjuku Antinoch on March 20, Koenji 20000VOLT on March 31 and Osaka's Juso Fandango on April 3, with sessions squeezed in at Afterbeat studio in Koenji.

years.src: Lambgoat: Zeni Geva · IDIOTEQ: From Tokyo flyers
yt: Zeni Geva and Albini at 20000V, March 31, 1992
years.h: Albini takes a guitar on stage at Koenji 20000VOLT
years.p: Zeni Geva and Albini cover Godflesh, recorded to 16 tracks in front of the crowd. It ends up on the 2026 box Superunit: Maximum Implosion.
years.xp:
The band released the Albini material under two names: "Zeni Geva & Steve Albini" for existing songs and "Superunit" for new ones with bassist MAS-P of Captain Condom. The bill also had Ruins and Volume Dealers. Albini brought his own microphones, a Veleno aluminum guitar, and a pool cue in a case with a Jesus Lizard sticker on it.

Big Black and Rapeman songs were kept out of the set. The other covers let Albini take vocals, including Kraftwerk's "The Model".

years.h: Albini switches off the dbx at Afterbeat
years.p: IDIOTEQ has him crouched under the console in Koenji, flipping switches until the studio's noise reduction was off. He objected to what it did to dynamic range.
years.xp: On the song "Shirushi" he pushed Null's vocals into distortion, borrowing a trick more common on home cassette recordings. Told that digital effects could do more, he insisted tape speed manipulation was the better route.

eras.title: Alternative Tentacles signs them
eras.text: Jello Biafra's Alternative Tentacles signed the band and put out two albums and a single, with Albini behind the board.

years.h: Jello Biafra's label gets its first Zeni Geva record, a 7-inch

years.src: Alternative Tentacles: Desire For Agony · Wikipedia: Desire for Agony · Wikipedia: Alternative Tentacles discography
yt: Stigma and Dead Sun Rising, live
years.h: Alternative Tentacles puts out Desire for Agony as Virus 135
years.p: The label calls it the band's full-length debut for them and one of the most extreme records in noise-core. Wikipedia lists a September 1993 session at The Basement in Chicago.
years.xp:
The album runs 38 minutes and 28 seconds. The cover painting is by Mark Fischer. Discogs dates the CD to 1994, while Wikipedia and the Alternative Tentacles discography say 1993.

AllMusic's Patrick Kennedy compared it to Motörhead meets King Crimson.

years.src: Wikipedia: Freedom Bondage · Monumental Movement: Zeni Geva
years.h: Freedom Bondage is recorded in France, with Albini again
years.p: Zeni Geva track it in June at Black Box studio, with Noro still on drums.
years.xp: The album is nine tracks and 38 minutes 32 seconds, ending with the 10:58 "Ground Zero". The Austin Chronicle reviewed it that November. Monumental Movement calls it the record where acoustic texture, structure and violence balance best.

eras.title: Noro out, a homemade machine in
eras.text: Noro left, and the songs stretched past ten minutes. Null started building his own electronics, and the band signed to Neurosis's label.

years.src: Wikipedia: Zeni Geva · Monumental Movement: Zeni Geva
years.h: Masataka Fujikake takes the drums from Eito Noro
years.p: Blake Fleming sits in briefly first. Monumental Movement credits Fujikake with adding polyrhythmic density.
years.xp: Fleming is listed by Wikipedia as a temporary drummer in 1996. A Zeni Geva show in Braunschweig that year is on YouTube.

years.src: Neurot Recordings: Deep Cut · Scaruffi: Zeni Geva
years.p: Albini records it at Electrical Audio in Chicago. Null layers static and distortion over the guitars with the nulltron, an instrument he built himself.
years.xp:
Neurot calls it the band's seventh album (catalog NR011, May 2001). Steve Von Till's pitch for the band: "one of the most punishing and relentlessly devastating bands to ever burst your skull open."

Scaruffi hears it as almost a parody of Zeni Geva, so opinions on the record run wide.

years.src: Wikipedia: Zeni Geva · Monumental Movement: Zeni Geva
years.h: A live album from Geneva, then Zeni Geva goes quiet
years.p: Last Nanosecond: Live in Geneva 2002 comes out in 2004. Null keeps releasing solo and collaborative work; Tabata works with Acid Mothers Temple.

eras.title: Yoshida comes back
eras.text: Tatsuya Yoshida returned on drums and the band toured again. The Albini recordings, and one of the labels that released them, kept surfacing.

years.cap: Zeni Geva at Supersonic Festival, Birmingham, October 24, 2010
years.src: Wikipedia: Zeni Geva · Monumental Movement: Zeni Geva
years.h: Tatsuya Yoshida comes back and Zeni Geva hit the road
years.p: A Tokyo show from March 2009 is on YouTube. The live album Alive and Rising, recorded that September, follows in 2010.

years.cap: Zeni Geva at the LUFF festival, Lausanne, autumn 2012
years.h: Tabata's exit leaves Null and Yoshida as a two-piece
years.p: They tour Europe that way. Total Castration is remastered and reissued the same year.

years.src: IDIOTEQ: From Tokyo flyers · Lambgoat: Zeni Geva
years.h: Skin Graft collects the Albini sessions on Superunit: Maximum Implosion
years.p: The Record Store Day double LP puts the 1992 Tokyo recordings together: the Nai-Ha album, studio tracks, and the live All Right, You Little Bastards!.
years.xp:
The set has a gatefold sleeve with photography by Mitsushiro Hiruma, a booklet, a pull-out poster, and Tabata's memoir The Future Belongs to Analog Loyalists. A riff from "Painwise" turned up later in Shellac's "The Guy Who Invented Fire".

Albini died on May 7, 2024, at Electrical Audio in Chicago, nine days before Shellac released To All Trains. He was 61.
